# `headmodel`

the gain of a spherical head model (MEG by Sarvas, three-shell EEG) on a source surface.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run headmodel --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run headmodel --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run headmodel --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels sensors --sources cortex --meg-surface inner_skull --eeg-surface scalp
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `channels` | manifold points, where {"name": "$channels"} | yes |
| `sources` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$sources"} | yes |
| `meg_surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$meg_surface"}, required false | no |
| `eeg_surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$eeg_surface"}, required false | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | `--channels` | none | - |  | the channels manifold (a points manifold with a 'type' labelling) by name |
| `sources` | `--sources` | none | - |  | the source surface by name: its vertices are the sources |
| `meg_surface` | `--meg-surface` | none | - |  | the surface the MEG spheres are fitted to (the inner skull) by name; null: no MEG model |
| `eeg_surface` | `--eeg-surface` | none | - |  | the surface the EEG sphere is fitted to (the scalp) by name; null: no EEG model |
| `name` | `--name` | `headmodel` | - |  | the gain's name; its source positions are <name>_GridLoc |
| `meg` | `--meg` | `overlapping_spheres` | - | overlapping_spheres, single_sphere, none | the MEG model: overlapping_spheres \| single_sphere \| none |
| `eeg` | `--eeg` | true | - |  | compute the EEG channels (three shells) |
| `project_electrodes` | `--project-electrodes` | true | - |  | move the electrodes radially onto the fitted EEG sphere |
| `sphere_cost` | `--sphere-cost` | `geometric` | - | geometric, algebraic | the sphere fit's cost: geometric \| algebraic |
| `sensor_weight_exponent` | `--sensor-weight-exponent` | `4.0` | - |  | the overlapping spheres' weight exponent p (w = sum \|weight\| d^-p) |
| `eeg_layers` | `--eeg-layers` | `brainstorm` | - | brainstorm, mne | the shells' radii and conductivities: brainstorm \| mne |
| `eeg_radii` | `--eeg-radii` | none | - |  | the shells' relative radii, innermost to outermost; null: the layers' |
| `eeg_conductivities` | `--eeg-conductivities` | none | S/m |  | the shells' conductivities, innermost to outermost; null: the layers' |
| `eeg_approximation` | `--eeg-approximation` | `berg_scherg` | - | berg_scherg, series | berg_scherg \| series |
| `eeg_series_terms` | `--eeg-series-terms` | none | - |  | the series' terms; null: the default |
| `berg_dipoles` | `--berg-dipoles` | none | - |  | the Berg-Scherg dipoles; null: the default |
| `berg_terms` | `--berg-terms` | none | - |  | the series terms the Berg-Scherg fit matches; null: the default |
| `berg_starts` | `--berg-starts` | none | - |  | the Berg-Scherg fit's simplex starts; null: the default |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.spherical_head_model`](../nodes.md) | channels=channels, sources=sources, meg_surface=meg_surface, eeg_surface=eeg_surface | meg=$meg, eeg=$eeg, project_electrodes=$project_electrodes, sphere_cost=$sphere_cost, sensor_weight_exponent=$sensor_weight_exponent, eeg_layers=$eeg_layers, eeg_radii=$eeg_radii, eeg_conductivities=$eeg_conductivities, eeg_approximation=$eeg_approximation, eeg_series_terms=$eeg_series_terms, berg_dipoles=$berg_dipoles, berg_terms=$berg_terms, berg_starts=$berg_starts | gain, grid |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `gain` | kind operator, operator_kind forward, name $name, from sources.manifold.0, to channels.manifold.0, acquisition_of channels |
| `grid` | kind field, kind_name GridLoc, name $name_GridLoc, on sources.manifold.0, of_operator gain |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE HEAD MODEL OF A SUBJECT IN SPHERES (an operator, the gain): MEG by Sarvas in one sphere fitted to the inner skull (single_sphere) or one sphere a sensor fitted to it
(overlapping_spheres, Brainstorm's default); EEG in three concentric shells fitted to the scalp (Berg-Scherg or the series), the electrodes moved onto the sphere. The sources are
the vertices of the source surface (x y z moments); the sensors are the channels' coils with their weights when stored, else one point a channel. The surfaces and the channels
are named by the caller (nothing is guessed): a model whose surface is not named is refused.
Stored: the gain `<name>` (an operator from the source surface, vector3, to the channels) and the source positions `<name>_GridLoc` (a field of it, in m).

  nxr-neuro run headmodel --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels sensors --sources cortex --meg-surface inner_skull --eeg-surface scalp
```
